## Classes

### <a name="proxmox_virtual_environment"></a>`proxmox_virtual_environment`

Writes a YAML file that the proxmox_virtual_environment providers read at runtime
to authenticate against the local PVE REST API. Declare this class on every
PVE node before declaring any pve_* resources.

#### Examples

##### Configure providers to use the local PVE API

```puppet
class { 'proxmox_virtual_environment':
  token_id        => 'puppet@pve!puppet',
  token_secret    => Sensitive(lookup('pve::token_secret')),
  cluster_manager => 'pve01.example.com',
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `proxmox_virtual_environment` class:

* [`token_id`](#-proxmox_virtual_environment--token_id)
* [`token_secret`](#-proxmox_virtual_environment--token_secret)
* [`cluster_manager`](#-proxmox_virtual_environment--cluster_manager)
* [`host`](#-proxmox_virtual_environment--host)
* [`port`](#-proxmox_virtual_environment--port)
* [`ssl_verify`](#-proxmox_virtual_environment--ssl_verify)
* [`ssl_ca_file`](#-proxmox_virtual_environment--ssl_ca_file)
* [`config_file`](#-proxmox_virtual_environment--config_file)

##### <a name="-proxmox_virtual_environment--token_id"></a>`token_id`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[^@!\s]+@[^@!\s]+![^!\s]+\z/]`

API token ID (format: user@realm!tokenname, e.g. root@pam!puppet).

##### <a name="-proxmox_virtual_environment--token_secret"></a>`token_secret`

Data type: `Sensitive[String]`

API token secret. Wrapped in Sensitive; never written to Puppet reports.

##### <a name="-proxmox_virtual_environment--cluster_manager"></a>`cluster_manager`

Data type: `String`

Puppet certname of the only node permitted to make PVE API changes.

##### <a name="-proxmox_virtual_environment--host"></a>`host`

Data type: `String`

PVE hostname or IP. Defaults to localhost (the PVE API on the same node).

Default value: `'localhost'`

##### <a name="-proxmox_virtual_environment--port"></a>`port`

Data type: `Integer`

PVE API port. Defaults to 8006.

Default value: `8006`

##### <a name="-proxmox_virtual_environment--ssl_verify"></a>`ssl_verify`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to verify the PVE TLS certificate. Defaults to true.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-proxmox_virtual_environment--ssl_ca_file"></a>`ssl_ca_file`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A\//]]`

Path to a CA certificate file when ssl_verify is true and PVE uses a private CA.
Passing undef explicitly disables the private-CA default and omits ssl_ca_file
from the rendered transport config.

Default value: `'/etc/pve/pve-root-ca.pem'`

##### <a name="-proxmox_virtual_environment--config_file"></a>`config_file`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A\//]`

Absolute path where the transport config YAML is written.
A symlink is created at the provider discovery path when this differs.
Defaults to the agent's own confdir (fact `proxmox_virtual_environment_confdir`), which is where
the providers look; the compiling server's confdir may differ.

Default value: `"${$facts['proxmox_virtual_environment_confdir'].lest || { $settings::confdir }}/pve_transport.yaml"`

### <a name="proxmox_virtual_environment--resources"></a>`proxmox_virtual_environment::resources`

Include this class after `proxmox_virtual_environment` when adopting an existing
PVE node or when you prefer data-driven resource declarations.

#### Examples

##### Declare resources from Hiera data

```puppet
include proxmox_virtual_environment::resources

# hiera.yaml data:
# proxmox_virtual_environment::resources::storages:
#   backup-nfs:
#     type: nfs
#     server: nfs.example.com
#     nfs_export: /srv/pve-backups
#     content: backup
```

##### Move a VXLAN zone to a new underlay, without applying it

```puppet
include proxmox_virtual_environment::resources

# hiera.yaml data:
# proxmox_virtual_environment::resources::sdn_zones:
#   zone1:
#     type: vxlan
#     peers: '10.0.0.1,10.0.0.2,10.0.0.3'
#     mtu: 1450
# proxmox_virtual_environment::resources::sdn_vnets:
#   vnet1:
#     zone: zone1
#     vnet_tag: 10100
# proxmox_virtual_environment::resources::sdn_subnets:
#   'vnet1|10.0.0.0/24':
#     gateway: '10.0.0.1'
#     snat: true
#
# The zone rewrite above is pending only. Report it on every run without
# touching the network:
# proxmox_virtual_environment::resources::sdn_apply:
#   sdn:
#     noop: true
```

Data type: `Hash[String, Hash]`

Hash of `pve_sdn_apply` resources. PVE has exactly one SDN configuration;
the only valid key is `sdn`. Declaring this opts in to applying pending SDN
changes, which reloads networking on every cluster node. Leave it empty to
keep SDN changes pending, or set `noop: true` to report them without
applying. See the SDN section of the README.

Default value: `{}`

### <a name="pve_acl"></a>`pve_acl`

Manages a Proxmox Virtual Environment ACL entry.

##### <a name="-pve_acl--acl_path"></a>`acl_path`

namevar

Data type: `String`

The ACL path (e.g. /, /storage/local).

##### <a name="-pve_acl--role"></a>`role`

namevar

Data type: `String`

The role to assign.

##### <a name="-pve_acl--ugid"></a>`ugid`

namevar

The user, group, or token ID this ACL applies to. Group principals are written with a leading @ (e.g. @admins), matching
PVE user.cfg syntax.

### <a name="pve_api_token"></a>`pve_api_token`

PVE returns a generated token secret only during creation. Set `secret_file` to
retain it on the Puppet agent without exposing it in reports or logs.

#### Examples

##### Create a token and retain its generated secret

```puppet
pve_api_token { 'automation@pve!ci':
  ensure      => present,
  privsep     => true,
  comment     => 'CI automation',
  secret_file => '/etc/puppetlabs/puppet/pve-ci-token.secret',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pve_api_token` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional human-readable comment.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PVE API property names to remove during an update.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this API token should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `expire`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Expiry as a Unix timestamp. 0 or unset means no expiry.

##### `privsep`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Restrict the token to a subset of its owning user permissions.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pve_api_token` type.

* [`secret_file`](#-pve_api_token--secret_file)
* [`tokenid`](#-pve_api_token--tokenid)

##### <a name="-pve_api_token--secret_file"></a>`secret_file`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Agent-local file receiving the one-time token secret on creation, written with mode 0600.

##### <a name="-pve_api_token--tokenid"></a>`tokenid`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Full token ID in user@realm!tokenname format.

### <a name="pve_backup_job"></a>`pve_backup_job`

Manages a scheduled Proxmox Virtual Environment vzdump backup job.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pve_backup_job` type.

##### `all`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Back up all guests.

##### `bwlimit`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

I/O bandwidth limit in KiB/s.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional human-readable comment.

##### `compress`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Compression algorithm.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PVE API property names to remove during an update.

##### `enabled`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Whether this backup job is enabled.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this backup job should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `exclude`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Array[Variant[String, Integer]]]]`

Guest IDs to exclude — either a comma-separated String (PVE property-string format) or an Array of IDs, which is joined into the property-string form before being sent to the API.

##### `fleecing`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Backup fleecing options in PVE property-string format (e.g. "enabled=1,storage=local-lvm"). VM only.

##### `job_schedule`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Calendar event schedule. Named job_schedule because schedule is reserved by Puppet.

##### `mailnotification`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['always', 'failure']]`

When to send legacy email notifications.

##### `mailto`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Notification email recipients.

##### `mode`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['snapshot', 'suspend', 'stop']]`

Backup mode.

##### `node`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Restrict the job to one cluster node.

##### `notes_template`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Template used for backup notes.

##### `notification_mode`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['auto', 'legacy-sendmail', 'notification-system']]`

Notification delivery mode.

##### `performance`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Performance-related settings in PVE property-string format (e.g. "max-workers=2,pbs-entries-max=1024").

##### `pool`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Restrict the job to a resource pool.

##### `protected`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Mark created backups as protected.

##### `prune_backups`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Retention options in PVE property-string format.

##### `repeat_missed`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Run missed jobs when the node becomes available.

##### `storage`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Target storage ID.

##### `vmid`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Array[Variant[String, Integer]]]]`

Guest IDs to include — either a comma-separated String (PVE property-string format) or an Array of IDs, which is joined into the property-string form before being sent to the API.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pve_backup_job` type.

* [`id`](#-pve_backup_job--id)

##### <a name="-pve_backup_job--id"></a>`id`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Unique backup job ID.

### <a name="pve_datacenter_config"></a>`pve_datacenter_config`

Manages the cluster-wide PVE datacenter configuration (datacenter.cfg),
exposed at GET/PUT /cluster/options. This is a singleton resource; declare
it with the title 'datacenter'.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pve_datacenter_config` type.

##### `bwlimit`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

I/O bandwidth limits in PVE property-string format (e.g. "default=10240,migration=5120").

##### `consent_text`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Consent text displayed before login.

##### `console`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['applet', 'vv', 'html5', 'xtermjs']]`

Default console viewer.

##### `crs`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Cluster resource scheduler settings in PVE property-string format.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PVE API property names to remove during an update.

##### `description`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Datacenter description shown in the web UI notes panel.

##### `email_from`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Email address used as the sender for notifications (defaults to root@$hostname).

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Keeps the datacenter configuration in sync. PVE rejects absent because it cannot be deleted.

Default value: `present`

##### `fencing`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['watchdog', 'hardware', 'both']]`

Fencing mode of the HA cluster.

##### `ha`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Cluster-wide HA settings in PVE property-string format (e.g. "shutdown_policy=migrate").

##### `http_proxy`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

HTTP proxy used by PVE for outgoing connections (e.g. http://proxy:8080).

##### `keyboard`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['de', 'de-ch', 'da', 'en-gb', 'en-us', 'es', 'fi', 'fr', 'fr-be', 'fr-ca', 'fr-ch', 'hu', 'is', 'it', 'ja', 'lt', 'mk', 'nl', 'no', 'pl', 'pt', 'pt-br', 'sv', 'sl', 'tr']]`

Default keyboard layout for the VNC console.

##### `language`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Default GUI language.

##### `mac_prefix`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Prefix for auto-generated guest MAC addresses (e.g. 'BC:24:11').

##### `max_workers`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Maximum number of workers per node for actions such as "stop all VMs".

##### `migration`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Cluster-wide migration settings in PVE property-string format (e.g. "type=secure,network=10.0.0.0/24").

##### `next_id`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Range for free VMID auto-selection in PVE property-string format (e.g. "lower=100,upper=1000000").

##### `notify_settings`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Cluster-wide notification settings in PVE property-string format.

##### `registered_tags`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

Tags that may only be set/removed by users with Sys.Modify on /.

##### `tag_style`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Tag display/sorting options in PVE property-string format (e.g. "shape=full,ordering=alphabetical").

##### `u2f`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

U2F configuration in PVE property-string format.

##### `user_tag_access`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Privilege options for user-settable tags in PVE property-string format (e.g. "user-allow=existing").

##### `webauthn`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

WebAuthn configuration in PVE property-string format (e.g. "rp=Example,origin=https://...,id=...").

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pve_datacenter_config` type.

* [`name`](#-pve_datacenter_config--name)

##### <a name="-pve_datacenter_config--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `Enum['datacenter']`

Must be 'datacenter'; PVE has exactly one cluster-wide configuration.

### <a name="pve_ha_resource"></a>`pve_ha_resource`

Manages Proxmox Virtual Environment HA resource membership — which guests the
HA manager keeps running, and how hard it tries.

Note this manages HA *membership*, not the guest's live power state. Setting
state to 'stopped' tells the HA manager to keep the guest stopped (and not
restart it after a node failure); it does not create or destroy the guest.
Removing the resource (ensure => absent) leaves the guest running exactly as
it is, merely unprotected.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pve_ha_resource` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional human-readable comment.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PVE API property names to remove during an update.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this guest should be under HA management.

Default value: `present`

##### `group`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

HA group restricting which nodes may run this guest. The group must already exist.

##### `max_relocate`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0]]`

How many times to try relocating the guest to another node after restarts are exhausted.

##### `max_restart`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0]]`

How many times to try restarting the guest on its current node before relocating it.

##### `state`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['started', 'stopped', 'disabled', 'ignored']]`

Requested HA state: started (run it, recover after node failure), stopped (keep down, still HA-managed), disabled (keep down, never start), ignored (entry kept, HA acts on nothing).

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pve_ha_resource` type.

* [`sid`](#-pve_ha_resource--sid)

##### <a name="-pve_ha_resource--sid"></a>`sid`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A(vm|ct):[0-9]+\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

HA service ID, including the guest-type prefix — e.g. 'vm:114' for a QEMU guest or 'ct:105' for a container.

### <a name="pve_sdn_apply"></a>`pve_sdn_apply`

Applies pending Proxmox Virtual Environment SDN configuration cluster-wide.

### Why this exists

Every other `pve_sdn_*` type writes to /etc/pve/sdn/*.cfg and changes
nothing on the wire. PVE only acts on those files when `PUT /cluster/sdn`
runs, which regenerates /etc/network/interfaces.d/sdn on **every** node and
reloads networking there. On a cluster carrying overlay guests that is a
disruptive operation, so no other resource in this module performs it, and
an agent run cannot trigger it as a side effect of an ordinary property
change.

Without this resource in the catalog, a zone whose `peers` list has been
rewritten reports green while the nodes keep forwarding on the old underlay
indefinitely. This resource closes that gap: it is out of sync whenever any
zone, VNet, subnet or controller differs from the applied running
configuration, and it names the offenders in `pending_objects`.

### Modes

```puppet
# Apply pending SDN changes during the agent run. Reloads networking
# cluster-wide, so only declare this where that is acceptable.
pve_sdn_apply { 'sdn': }

# Report unapplied SDN changes on every run and never touch the network.
# Puppet's own noop metaparameter; the run stays corrective-free.
pve_sdn_apply { 'sdn':
  noop => true,
}
```

Not declaring it at all leaves the module unable to apply anything, which is
the default.

### Ordering

This type automatically requires every `pve_sdn_*` resource in the catalog,
so it observes the writes made earlier in the same run.

### Failure reporting

`PUT /cluster/sdn` returns a UPID for a background worker. By default this
resource waits for that worker and fails the resource unless it exits `OK`;
otherwise a failed apply would be reported as a successful change. Set
`wait => false` to fire and forget.

### One-off apply

The `proxmox_virtual_environment::sdn_apply` Bolt task performs the same
apply without a catalog, for use in a maintenance window.

### IPAM and DNS

`pve_sdn_ipam` and `pve_sdn_dns` are not part of the pending/running split
and take effect immediately, so they are deliberately not counted here.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pve_sdn_apply` type.

##### `applied`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the SDN running configuration matches the configured one. Only true is meaningful to declare; it is the default.

Default value: `true`

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Always present. This resource represents an action on the existing SDN configuration, not an object, so absent is rejected.

Default value: `present`

##### `pending_objects`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

Read-only. SDN objects that differ from the running configuration, as "<kind>/<id>: <state>" entries, e.g. "zones/zone1: changed".

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pve_sdn_apply` type.

* [`name`](#-pve_sdn_apply--name)
* [`timeout`](#-pve_sdn_apply--timeout)
* [`wait`](#-pve_sdn_apply--wait)

##### <a name="-pve_sdn_apply--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `Enum['sdn']`

Singleton name. PVE has exactly one SDN configuration, so the only valid title is 'sdn'.

##### <a name="-pve_sdn_apply--timeout"></a>`timeout`

Data type: `Integer`

Seconds to wait for the apply worker task before giving up.

Default value: `300`

##### <a name="-pve_sdn_apply--wait"></a>`wait`

Data type: `Boolean`

Wait for the apply worker task to finish and fail the resource unless it exits OK.

Default value: `true`

### <a name="pve_sdn_controller"></a>`pve_sdn_controller`

Manages a Proxmox Virtual Environment SDN controller.

Controllers drive the routing daemon (FRR) for EVPN, BGP and IS-IS zones.
An evpn zone requires one.

**This resource writes pending configuration only.** A change here lands in
/etc/pve/sdn/controllers.cfg and alters nothing on the wire until the
separate `PUT /cluster/sdn` apply runs. This type never performs that apply;
declare `pve_sdn_apply` to opt in, or `pve_sdn_apply { 'sdn': noop => true }`
to have every run report unapplied changes without touching the network.

Attributes are grouped by the plugin type that accepts them.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pve_sdn_controller` type.

##### `asn`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Autonomous system number.

##### `bgp_mode`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['auto', 'external', 'internal']]`

Whether to use eBGP or iBGP. Auto decides from the BGP controller and falls back to iBGP.

##### `bgp_multipath_as_path_relax`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Consider AS paths of equal length but differing content for multipath.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PVE API property names to remove during an update.

##### `ebgp`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Use eBGP (remote-as external) rather than iBGP.

##### `ebgp_multihop`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Maximum hop count for eBGP peers.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this SDN controller should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `fabric`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

SDN fabric used as the underlay for this EVPN controller. Fabrics themselves are not managed by this module; the name is passed through to PVE.

##### `isis_domain`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the IS-IS domain.

##### `isis_ifaces`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated list of interfaces on which IS-IS is active. Compared as an unordered set.

##### `isis_net`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Network entity title for this node in the IS-IS network.

##### `loopback`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Loopback or dummy interface providing the router IP.

##### `node`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Cluster node this BGP controller configures. A bgp controller is per-node.

##### `nodes`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated list of cluster nodes this controller applies to. Compared as an unordered set.

##### `peer_group_name`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the BGP peer group for this EVPN controller. Defaults to VTEP.

##### `peers`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated list of BGP peer addresses. Compared as an unordered set.

##### `pending_state`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['new', 'changed', 'deleted']]`

Read-only. Whether this controller differs from the applied running configuration. Absent means the controller is applied.

##### `route_map_in`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Route map applied to incoming routes. Route maps themselves are not managed by this module.

##### `route_map_out`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Route map applied to outgoing routes. Route maps themselves are not managed by this module.

##### `type`

Data type: `Enum['evpn', 'bgp', 'isis', 'faucet']`

Controller plugin type. Cannot be changed after creation. The faucet plugin is experimental and unmaintained upstream.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pve_sdn_controller` type.

* [`controller`](#-pve_sdn_controller--controller)

##### <a name="-pve_sdn_controller--controller"></a>`controller`

namevar

Data type: `String[1,64]`

The SDN controller identifier.

### <a name="pve_sdn_dns"></a>`pve_sdn_dns`

Manages a Proxmox Virtual Environment SDN DNS backend.

**Unlike the other SDN types, this one needs no apply.** DNS backends are
not part of the pending/running split: `/cluster/sdn/dns` accepts neither
`pending` nor `running`, there is no dns section in
/etc/pve/sdn/.running-config, and PVE calls the backend live when it
registers a record. A change here takes effect immediately, so this type has
no `pending_state` property and `pve_sdn_apply` ignores it.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pve_sdn_dns` type.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PVE API property names to remove during an update.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this DNS backend should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `fingerprint`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

SHA-256 fingerprint of the PowerDNS TLS certificate, for a private CA.

##### `key`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

PowerDNS API key. PVE stores it in cleartext in /etc/pve/sdn/dns.cfg and returns it, so it is compared directly and drift is detected. Redacted from Puppet reports.

##### `reversemaskv6`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Prefix length used when generating IPv6 reverse zones.

##### `ttl`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

TTL applied to records this backend creates.

##### `type`

Data type: `Enum['powerdns']`

DNS plugin type. Cannot be changed after creation. PowerDNS is the only backend PVE implements.

##### `url`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

PowerDNS API URL, e.g. http://powerdns.example.com:8081/api/v1/servers/localhost. Required by PVE when creating the backend.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pve_sdn_dns` type.

* [`dns`](#-pve_sdn_dns--dns)

##### <a name="-pve_sdn_dns--dns"></a>`dns`

namevar

Data type: `String`

The SDN DNS identifier.

### <a name="pve_sdn_ipam"></a>`pve_sdn_ipam`

Manages a Proxmox Virtual Environment SDN IPAM backend.

**Unlike the other SDN types, this one needs no apply.** IPAM backends are
not part of the pending/running split: `/cluster/sdn/ipams` accepts neither
`pending` nor `running`, there is no ipams section in

allocates an address. A change here takes effect immediately, so this type

PVE always provides a built-in `pve` IPAM. Declare this type only for an

Data type: `Enum['pve', 'netbox', 'phpipam']`

##### `url`

### <a name="pve_sdn_subnet"></a>`pve_sdn_subnet`

Manages a Proxmox Virtual Environment SDN subnet.

**This resource writes pending configuration only.** A change here lands in
/etc/pve/sdn/subnets.cfg and alters nothing on the wire until the separate
`PUT /cluster/sdn` apply runs. This type never performs that apply; declare
`pve_sdn_apply` to opt in, or `pve_sdn_apply { 'sdn': noop => true }` to have
every run report unapplied changes without touching the network.

### Identity

Subnets are nested under a VNet, and PVE does not use the CIDR as the object
identifier. It derives one by prefixing the VNet's zone and replacing the
slash with a dash, so `10.0.0.0/24` in a VNet belonging to zone `zone1`
becomes `zone1-10.0.0.0-24`. Only the create endpoint accepts a bare CIDR;
update and delete address the derived identifier.

This type is therefore keyed by VNet and CIDR, written as a pipe-separated
title in the same style as `pve_acl`. The provider resolves the VNet's zone
and derives the PVE identifier itself, and reports it back in the read-only
`subnet_id` property.

```puppet
pve_sdn_subnet { 'vnet1|10.0.0.0/24':
  gateway => '10.0.0.1',
  snat    => true,
}
```

Changing the CIDR of an existing subnet is a delete and a create, not an
update: the CIDR is part of the identity.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pve_sdn_subnet` type.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PVE API property names to remove during an update.

##### `dhcp_dns_server`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

DNS server address handed out to DHCP clients in this subnet.

##### `dhcp_range`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

DHCP ranges as PVE property strings, e.g. 'start-address=10.0.0.100,end-address=10.0.0.200'. PVE returns them expanded and reordered, so they compare as an unordered set.

##### `dnszoneprefix`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

DNS prefix inserted before the zone's domain, e.g. 'adm' yields <hostname>.adm.example.com.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this SDN subnet should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `gateway`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Gateway address for this subnet. Assigned to the VNet interface in layer 3 zones.

##### `pending_state`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['new', 'changed', 'deleted']]`

Read-only. Whether this subnet differs from the applied running configuration. Absent means the subnet is applied.

##### `snat`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Masquerade traffic leaving this subnet. Requires the PVE firewall.

##### `subnet_id`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Read-only. The identifier PVE derived for this subnet, e.g. zone1-10.0.0.0-24.

##### `type`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['subnet']]`

Object type. PVE only defines "subnet" here. Cannot be changed after creation.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pve_sdn_subnet` type.

* [`cidr`](#-pve_sdn_subnet--cidr)
* [`vnet`](#-pve_sdn_subnet--vnet)

##### <a name="-pve_sdn_subnet--cidr"></a>`cidr`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Subnet in CIDR notation, e.g. 10.0.0.0/24. Part of the identity: changing it replaces the subnet.

##### <a name="-pve_sdn_subnet--vnet"></a>`vnet`

namevar

Data type: `String[1,8]`

VNet this subnet belongs to.

### <a name="pve_sdn_vnet"></a>`pve_sdn_vnet`

Manages a Proxmox Virtual Environment SDN VNet.

**This resource writes pending configuration only.** A change here lands in
/etc/pve/sdn/vnets.cfg and alters nothing on the wire until the separate
`PUT /cluster/sdn` apply runs. This type never performs that apply; declare
`pve_sdn_apply` to opt in, or `pve_sdn_apply { 'sdn': noop => true }` to have
every run report unapplied changes without touching the network.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pve_sdn_vnet` type.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PVE API property names to remove during an update.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this SDN VNet should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `isolate_ports`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Set the isolated flag on every interface attached to this VNet bridge, preventing guest-to-guest traffic within the VNet.

##### `pending_state`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['new', 'changed', 'deleted']]`

Read-only. Whether this VNet differs from the applied running configuration. Absent means the VNet is applied.

##### `type`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['vnet']]`

Object type. PVE only defines "vnet" here; it exists for symmetry with the other SDN types and cannot be changed after creation.

##### `vlanaware`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Allow VLAN-tagged traffic to pass through this VNet.

##### `vnet_alias`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Human-readable alias for this VNet. Maps to PVE's `alias`; Puppet reserves that name as a metaparameter.

##### `vnet_tag`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

VLAN tag for vlan and qinq zones, or the VXLAN VNI for vxlan and evpn zones. Maps to PVE's `tag`; Puppet reserves that name as a metaparameter.

##### `zone`

Data type: `String`

Zone this VNet belongs to. PVE permits moving a VNet between zones, so this is an ordinary property rather than an immutable one.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pve_sdn_vnet` type.

* [`vnet`](#-pve_sdn_vnet--vnet)

##### <a name="-pve_sdn_vnet--vnet"></a>`vnet`

namevar

Data type: `String[1,8]`

The SDN VNet identifier. PVE limits this to 8 characters.

### <a name="pve_sdn_zone"></a>`pve_sdn_zone`

Manages a Proxmox Virtual Environment SDN zone.

**This resource writes pending configuration only.** A change here lands in
/etc/pve/sdn/zones.cfg and alters nothing on the wire. PVE only regenerates
/etc/network/interfaces.d/sdn and reloads networking when the separate
`PUT /cluster/sdn` apply runs, which this type never performs -- an implicit
apply on an ordinary agent run would blip every overlay guest in the cluster.

Declare `pve_sdn_apply` to opt in to applying, or `pve_sdn_apply` with
`noop => true` to have every run report unapplied changes without touching
the network. The read-only `pending_state` property below shows the same
thing per zone.

Attributes are grouped by the plugin type that accepts them; PVE rejects an
attribute that does not belong to the zone's type.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pve_sdn_zone` type.

##### `advertise_subnets`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Advertise IP prefixes as EVPN type-5 routes instead of MAC/IP pairs as type-2 routes.

##### `bridge`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Bridge whose VLANs this zone manages. Required for vlan and qinq zones.

##### `bridge_disable_mac_learning`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Disable automatic MAC learning on the zone bridge.

##### `controller`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

EVPN controller for this zone (see pve_sdn_controller). Required for evpn zones.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PVE API property names to remove during an update.

##### `dhcp`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['dnsmasq']]`

DHCP backend for this zone. Requires subnets with a dhcp_range.

##### `disable_arp_nd_suppression`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Stop suppressing IPv4 ARP and IPv6 neighbour discovery messages.

##### `dns`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

DNS API server used to register guest records (see pve_sdn_dns).

##### `dnszone`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

DNS domain for registered records, e.g. example.com.

##### `dp_id`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Faucet dataplane ID. Only meaningful for the experimental faucet plugin.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this SDN zone should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `exitnodes`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated list of nodes acting as EVPN exit nodes. Compared as an unordered set.

##### `exitnodes_local_routing`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Allow exit nodes to reach EVPN guests locally.

##### `exitnodes_primary`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Force egress traffic through this exit node first.

##### `fabric`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

SDN fabric used as the underlay for this zone. Fabrics themselves are not managed by this module; the name is passed through to PVE.

##### `ipam`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

IPAM backend used for address allocation in this zone (see pve_sdn_ipam). PVE uses the built-in "pve" IPAM when unset.

##### `mac`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Anycast MAC address of the logical router.

##### `mtu`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

MTU applied to the VNet bridges created for this zone.

##### `nodes`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated list of cluster nodes this zone is deployed on. Compared as an unordered set.

##### `peers`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated list of VTEP peer addresses, usually the underlay IPs of the cluster nodes. Required for vxlan zones. Compared as an unordered set.

##### `pending_state`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['new', 'changed', 'deleted']]`

Read-only. Whether this zone differs from the applied running configuration; absent means applied. Never enforced -- it makes an unapplied change visible in reports.

##### `reversedns`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

DNS API server used to register reverse records.

##### `rt_import`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated list of route targets to import into the zone VRF. Compared as an unordered set.

##### `secondary_controllers`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

Additional controllers for this zone. Compared as an unordered set.

##### `service_vlan`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Service-VLAN tag (the outer VLAN). Required for qinq zones. Maps to PVE's `tag`, which cannot be used as an attribute name because Puppet reserves it as a metaparameter.

##### `type`

Data type: `Enum['simple', 'vlan', 'qinq', 'vxlan', 'evpn', 'faucet']`

Zone plugin type. Cannot be changed after creation. The faucet plugin is experimental and unmaintained upstream.

##### `vlan_protocol`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['802.1q', '802.1ad']]`

Encapsulation protocol for the qinq service VLAN. Defaults to 802.1q.

##### `vrf_vxlan`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

VNI of the zone VRF. Required for evpn zones, and must not collide with any VNet tag.

##### `vxlan_port`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

UDP port for the VXLAN tunnel. Defaults to 4789.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pve_sdn_zone` type.

* [`zone`](#-pve_sdn_zone--zone)

##### <a name="-pve_sdn_zone--zone"></a>`zone`

namevar

Data type: `String[1,8]`

The SDN zone identifier. PVE limits this to 8 characters.

### <a name="pve_storage"></a>`pve_storage`

Manages a Proxmox Virtual Environment storage definition.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pve_storage` type.

##### `blocksize`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

ZFS block size (a power of 2, optionally suffixed with k or m). Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `bwlimit`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

I/O bandwidth limits in PVE property-string format (e.g. "restore=10240,migration=5120"), in KiB/s.

##### `content`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated list of allowed content types.

##### `create_base_path`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Create the base directory if it does not exist. Defaults to true.

##### `create_subdirs`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Populate the directory with the default content-type subdirectory structure. Defaults to true.

##### `data_pool`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Ceph data pool used for erasure coding.

##### `datastore`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Proxmox Backup Server datastore name. Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PVE API property names to remove during an update.

##### `disable`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Disable this storage.

##### `encryption_key`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

Encryption key for PBS storages as a JSON string, or "autogen" to generate one. Compared by the key fingerprint PVE reports; "autogen" only requires that some key exists.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this storage definition should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `fingerprint`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Remote TLS certificate fingerprint.

##### `is_mountpoint`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Path PVE should treat as an externally managed mountpoint, or "yes"/"no" to use the storage path as a shortcut.

##### `keyring`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Ceph client keyring contents (for external clusters).

##### `krbd`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Always access RBD storage through the krbd kernel module.

##### `max_protected_backups`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Maximum number of protected backups per guest.

##### `monhost`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated list of Ceph monitor IP addresses (for external clusters).

##### `mountpoint`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Mount point for applicable storage backends.

##### `namespace`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Proxmox Backup Server namespace.

##### `nfs_export`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

NFS export path. Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `nocow`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Set the NOCOW flag on files, disabling data checksumming. Only use on storage that is otherwise protected against bitrot.

##### `nodes`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated list of nodes allowed to use this storage.

##### `options`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Backend-specific mount options.

##### `password`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

Remote storage password. PVE never returns it, so it is compared against /etc/pve/priv/storage/<id>.pw; requires the agent to run on the PVE node as root.

##### `path`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Filesystem path for directory-like storage backends. Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `pool`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Ceph or ZFS pool name. Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `portal`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

iSCSI portal. Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `preallocation`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['off', 'metadata', 'falloc', 'full']]`

Preallocation mode for raw and qcow2 images. Defaults to metadata.

##### `prune_backups`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Backup retention options in PVE property-string format.

##### `server`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Remote server for network storage. Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `share`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

CIFS share name. Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `shared`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Mark this storage as shared between nodes.

##### `skip_cert_verification`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Skip remote TLS certificate verification.

##### `sparse`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Use sparse volumes.

##### `subdir`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Subdirectory to use on the backend.

##### `target`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

iSCSI target. Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `thinpool`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

LVM thin pool name. Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `type`

Data type: `Enum['btrfs', 'cephfs', 'cifs', 'dir', 'esxi', 'iscsi', 'iscsidirect', 'lvm', 'lvmthin', 'nfs', 'pbs', 'rbd', 'zfs', 'zfspool']`

Storage backend type. Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `username`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Remote storage username.

##### `vgname`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

LVM volume group name. Cannot be changed after creation.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pve_storage` type.

* [`storage`](#-pve_storage--storage)

##### <a name="-pve_storage--storage"></a>`storage`

namevar

Data type: `String`

The PVE storage ID.

### <a name="pve_user"></a>`pve_user`

Manages a Proxmox Virtual Environment user.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pve_user` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional human-readable comment.

##### `email`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Email address of the user.

##### `enable`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the user account is enabled.

Default value: `true`

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this user should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `expire`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Account expiry time as a Unix timestamp (0 means no expiry).

##### `firstname`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

First name of the user.

##### `groups`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated list of PVE groups.

##### `keys`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

User public keys.

##### `lastname`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Last name of the user.

##### `password`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

User password. Sent on creation; changes are applied with "pveum passwd" because PVE refuses API-token auth on PUT /access/password. Compared against /etc/pve/priv/shadow.cfg.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pve_user` type.

* [`userid`](#-pve_user--userid)

##### <a name="-pve_user--userid"></a>`userid`

namevar

Data type: `String`

The user ID in user@realm format.

## Tasks

### <a name="pve_api_request"></a>`pve_api_request`

Call any Proxmox Virtual Environment API endpoint exposed by /api2/json.

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `host`

Data type: `String[1]`

PVE host name or IP address.

##### `port`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1, 65535]]`

PVE API port.

##### `token_id`

Data type: `String[1]`

PVE API token ID, for example puppet@pve!puppet-token.

##### `token_secret`

Data type: `Sensitive[String[1]]`

PVE API token secret.

##### `method`

Data type: `Enum['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE']`

HTTP method.

##### `path`

Data type: `Pattern[/^\//]`

API path below /api2/json, for example /version or /storage/{storage}.

##### `path_params`

Data type: `Optional[Hash[String, Any]]`

Path template values for placeholders such as {name}.

##### `query`

Data type: `Optional[Hash[String, Any]]`

Query string parameters.

##### `body`

Data type: `Optional[Hash[String, Any]]`

JSON request body parameters.

##### `ssl_verify`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Verify the PVE TLS certificate.

##### `ssl_ca_file`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Optional CA bundle path.

### <a name="sdn_apply"></a>`sdn_apply`

Apply pending Proxmox Virtual Environment SDN configuration cluster-wide. Regenerates /etc/network/interfaces.d/sdn on every node and reloads networking there, so run it in a maintenance window. Use dry_run first to preview the change.

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `host`

Data type: `String[1]`

PVE host name or IP address.

##### `port`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1, 65535]]`

PVE API port.

##### `token_id`

Data type: `String[1]`

PVE API token ID, for example puppet@pve!puppet-token.

##### `token_secret`

Data type: `Sensitive[String[1]]`

PVE API token secret.

##### `dry_run`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Preview the change instead of applying it. Returns the interfaces and FRR diffs for the given node without touching anything. Requires node.

##### `node`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Cluster node to compute the dry-run diff for. Only used with dry_run.

##### `wait`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Wait for the apply worker task and fail unless it exits OK. Defaults to true.

##### `timeout`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1]]`

Seconds to wait for the apply worker task. Defaults to 300.

##### `ssl_verify`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Verify the PVE TLS certificate.

##### `ssl_ca_file`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Optional CA bundle path.
